items: Inference never backtracks once a candidate set is chosen.
T from `A | B` yields the union, as expected.
Inferring INTO `T | null` tries each member.
It can pick a surprising one and stop there.

lines: type Debug<T> = T
const _: Debug<never> = someValue
// error message prints the resolved type
const cfg = { ... } satisfies Config

items: Hover first; force an error when hover is not enough.
`satisfies` (4.9) validates but keeps the narrow type.
It pairs well with generics at config boundaries.
`any` disables checking; `unknown` loses the relation.
Only a generic preserves input-to-output.
Overloads give per-case returns and completion.
But overloads break `infer`-based utilities.
Interface + generic: erased, free at runtime.
Abstract class: runtime cost, shared implementation.
Types cannot check data — validate, then re-enter types.

blocks.title: Cost Is Per Editor Keystroke
blocks.text: Slow types are not a build problem only — the language server re-runs the same instantiations while you type.

items: Deep conditionals cost O(depth) instantiations.
Then: 'Type instantiation is excessively deep'.
Type-level string parsing and arithmetic are legal.
A route parser can add seconds per keystroke.

lines: tsc --diagnostics
tsc --extendedDiagnostics  // check time
tsc --generateTrace out/     // per-type cost

items: They report instantiation counts and check time.
Usual fixes: variance annotations, shallower utilities.
A five-level conditional is unmaintainable by others.
An overload set or plain union is often better engineering.

blocks.title: Proportionality Heuristic
blocks.text: Generic complexity should match how many callers benefit. Library boundaries earn it; one-off application code rarely does.

lines: function log<T>(msg: string) {}  // T unused
function parse<T>(s: string): T  // a cast
// caller names T, compiler verifies nothing

items: Unused T becomes unknown; no warning without a lint rule.
Return-only generics are disguised casts.
Return `unknown` and make the caller narrow.
Three parameters where one interface would do is worse.
A constrained T may add extra required members.
So a bound-shaped literal will not assign to T.
`{}` and `object` are not 'any object'.
`{}` accepts string and number, all but null/undefined.

lines: type NonEmpty<T> = T extends [] ? never : T
// odd on unions until you wrap it:
type NonEmpty2<T> = [T] extends [[]] ? never : T
// never in, never out is the rule, not a bug

items: ReturnType on overloads resolves the last signature.
Parameters on overloads does the same.
Array covariance: `const animals: Animal[] = dogs`, then push.
Compiles, corrupts. Use `readonly Animal[]` to read.
`as any` inside a generic body makes the signature lie.
Isolate it to one line with a comment saying why.
Turn on `strictFunctionTypes`.
Turn on `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`.
Container code is where both flags earn their keep.

blocks.title: Cheapest Review Question
blocks.text: Ask of every type parameter: what relationship does this carry? No answer means delete it.

lines: function f<T>(x: T): T            // declare
function g<T extends Bound>(x: T)  // constrain
type H<T = Fallback> = T           // default
type I<T extends B = D> = T        // both

items: Works on functions, classes, interfaces, aliases.
Constrain when the body needs members.
Return T, never the constraint.
That is how the caller keeps its literal type.
Arguments are read left to right.
Conflicting candidates union instead of erroring.
Explicit args skip the check inference would run.

lines: function get<T, K extends keyof T>(
o: T, k: K
): T[K] { return o[k] }
// most reusable generic in app code
T extends U ? X : Y      // distributes if naked
[T] extends [U] ? X : Y  // stops distribution
T extends [infer H, ...infer R] ? H : never

items: `never` in, `never` out — the empty union runs nothing.
`infer` is legal in the `extends` clause only.
Covariant sites union, contravariant sites intersect.

lines: { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] }        // add optional
{ readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] } // add readonly
{ [K in keyof T as `on${K & string}`]: Fn }

items: Homomorphic mapping preserves arrays, tuples, modifiers.
Arrays are unsoundly covariant; methods stay bivariant.
Annotate variance for checker speed, not behaviour.
Budget: depth ~50, ~1000 with tail recursion.

blocks.title: Final Principle
blocks.text: Generics move relationships out of comments and into the compiler. Every type parameter should carry one; a parameter that carries none should be deleted.

caption.text: Part 2 of TYPESCRIPT GENERICS. `any` compiles and then crashes at 3am — a generic is how you tell the compiler that two positions in a signature are the SAME type. Ten pages on the mechanics tsc actually runs: inference candidates and widening, constraints as a two-sided bargain, conditional types that distribute over unions, `infer` pattern matching, mapped-type remapping, and the variance rules that decide when F<Dog> fits F<Animal>. Ends with a cheat sheet worth screenshotting.
